chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar narrated from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them, who said:

I asked him about a man who married a woman but did not consummate the marriage, and then committed adultery—what is upon him? He said: "He is to be lashed with the prescribed punishment, his head is to be shaved, he is to be separated from his wife, and he is to be exiled for one year."

key_terms.فَلَمْ يَدْخُلْ بِهَا: did not consummate the marriage with her
key_terms.وَيُحْلَقُ رَأْسُهُ: his head is to be shaved
key_terms.وَيُفَرَّقُ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ أَهْلِهِ: he is to be separated from his family
key_terms.وَيُنْفَى سَنَةً: he is to be exiled for one year

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a married man who committed zina before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a man who has married but has not consummated the marriage, then commits zina. The Imam عليه السلام states that the punishment includes the hadd, shaving the head, separation from his family, and exile for one year, indicating a jurisprudential ruling tied to marriage and criminal law.
